title: Advisory agent-process re-review
nature: advisory; not a phase gate (no gate_conformance/gate_status and no docs/implementation/phase-26/phase-review.json)
scope: The Phase 26 harness change set landed by tasks 26.1-26.5: the additive phase-21 orchestration amendment (26.1); the docs/agent-contracts.md rules A1-A7 (26.2); the scripts/check-agents.sh guards (26.3); the seven/eight .opencode/agents prompt corrections (26.4); and the .opencode/scripts/collect-session-usage.sh fix (26.5). It re-reviews the classes recorded as agent_process observations in the v1.2 release review, the phase-20 phase review (base and attempt-2), and the named Phase 21 task records.
method: Read the actual agent_process.observations from docs/implementation/final-review/release-review-v1.2.json, docs/implementation/phase-20/phase-review.json, docs/implementation/phase-20/phase-review.attempt-2.json and the 21.5/21.7/21.9/21.13 finding records; read the changed harness files themselves (docs/agent-contracts.md, scripts/check-agents.sh, the eight .opencode/agents prompts, .opencode/scripts/collect-session-usage.sh); classified each distinct observation as enforced-by-guard (citing the exact scripts/check-agents.sh location), prompt-rule (citing the exact prompt/contract line), or uncovered; then ran scripts/check-agents.sh and scripts/check-docs.sh once. Every closure below was verified against the file, not taken from the task reports.

summary: The Phase 26 guards now cover the previously advisory classes that are mechanically checkable, and the remaining classes are stated rules rather than silent gaps. Of the distinct v1.2 process observations re-checked here, one cluster - phase-level aggregate consistency - is genuinely enforced by scripts/check-agents.sh:309-463 (numeric sums, subagents shape, and phase-reviewer presence/equality, with scope self-checks at :240-250); the rest are prompt-rule closures: the superseded-identity sweep, the security-disposition gate obligation, unbatched re-derivation, orchestrator-run specialist tasks, attempt-0 retry/final-task record, stale suite baselines, reviewer-reads-owning-criterion, planner criteria superset, isolated destructive probes, causal-claim checking, planner content-loss, and live-verifier terminality. Two items are honestly outside the guard/rule taxonomy: the collector observation was resolved by direct tool repair (task 26.5), and two clauses of the aggregate observation (aggregate.note dangling-reference detection and first-pass-rate recomputation) remain unenforced. No observation was found to be silently unaddressed. Residuals are recorded in `limitations`; none is a phase blocker, and this record holds nothing open because it is advisory.
limitations: Most closed classes are prompt/contract-only and cannot be mechanically checked: a superseded-hash sweep, a security disposition, an unbatched re-derivation, an orchestrator-run declaration, a causal-claim check, a planner-superset criterion, and a live-verifier terminal status all depend on agent behavior, so the guards cannot prove they were followed. The guard only proves the record shapes it can parse.

The aggregate guard is enforced from phase 26 only. Phases 20-25 are grandfathered as immutable history, so the stale phase-20 aggregate that motivated the observation is not re-checked (it was reconciled in the Phase 20 gate commit).

The phase-26 aggregate branch has not yet been exercised by real data: docs/implementation/phase-26/orchestration.json does not exist at this review, so the branch is exercised only by the 26.3 reviewer's fabricated conforming fixture. Its first real exercise is the Phase 26 gate record; the guard should be re-run once that record exists (the 26.3 reviewer recorded the same reason).

scripts/check-agents.sh:340 explicitly excludes first_pass_approval_rate and note from recomputation; the phase-20 attempt-2 observation's proposed dangling-section-reference check was not implemented. Both are listed in `uncovered`.
The no-build/rebuild clause (docs/agent-contracts.md:70-71) has no counterpart in any .opencode/agents prompt; an agent that reads only its prompt, not the contract, would not see it.

The Enforcement scope preamble (docs/agent-contracts.md:127-130) still reads 'phase records at phase 20 and later' while the section now contains a from-phase-26 bullet; the from-phase-26 bullet is explicit so the self-checks pass and there is no guard drift, but the preamble wording is imprecise (the 26.2 reviewer flagged this as F1 and it was not rephrased in 26.3).
docs/agent-contracts.md sits exactly at its 220-line budget (wc -l = 220), so the next contract addition will require a budget raise or a condense.

The two scope self-checks (scripts/check-agents.sh:240-250) are bare phrase greps, so they fail only on absence, not on disagreement: lowering AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE to 20 still passes because the contract contains 'from phase 20' for other rules (26.3 test-quality finding F-26.3-TQ-09). The undetected direction enforces more than the contract states, not less.

This record is itself advisory and was not gated by an independent reviewer, consistent with the planning record's note that task 26.6's review is the orchestrator's and the record holds nothing open.
